description: The article presents a refined bottom-up coding scheme of students' LLM use, derived iteratively from LLM-use reports in a research-oriented course and cross-labeled by student initiative.
title: A bottom-up taxonomy of seven student LLM usage categories organized into three support types

description: The article outlines a process for evaluating content alignment that is sensitive to the particular ways computerized adaptive tests can diverge from their intended content domain.
title: A CAT-sensitive process for evaluating content alignment

description: The article proposes a taxonomy of the semantic landscape of concreteness and abstraction in mathematics education, built from qualitative coding of a corpus of 368 papers.
title: A data-driven taxonomy organizing the meanings of concrete and abstract along a learner–representation–concept dimension

description: The article introduces a structured methodology for evaluating educational innovations' conceptual foundations, developed through practice at the International Centre for EdTech Impact.
title: A five-step systematic methodology for building the conceptual evidence base of educational innovations

description: The article develops a health care setting-adapted version of cognitive task analysis, a suite of methods for studying cognitive processes such as reasoning, problem-solving, and decision-making.
title: A four-step adapted cognitive task analysis framework for clinical environments

description: The editorial describes a shared evaluation process modeled by every article in the special issue.
title: A four-step evaluative framework for judging educational practices and beliefs

description: The guide presents an organizing framework of four evidence types that educators encounter when evaluating product effectiveness claims.
title: A four-type hierarchy of evidence for judging educational technology effectiveness

description: The special issue's theoretical backbone distinguishes promotive effects (factors benefiting all learners), protective effects (factors offsetting risk), and compensatory mechanisms.
title: A framework and operationalization of study designs and statistical approaches for studying academic resilience in literacy

description: The article introduces a fine-grained taxonomy categorizing novice programmers' difficulties with reading control flow constructs.
title: A hierarchical taxonomy of novice difficulties with selection and iteration in code reading

description: The paper argues that researchers should articulate their causal assumptions graphically before collecting or analyzing data, because \"there are no causal conclusions without causal assumptions\".
title: A priori causal-graph specification before educational data analysis

description: The article recommends planning replications inside multi-year research programs rather than as one-off studies: \"a logical next step for our research on ROOTS would be to conduct a series of increasingly distal replication studies.\" It reports grounding its IES-funded ROOTS efficacy project in a sy
title: A priori systematic replication-series planning with treatment-response rates

description: The article distinguishes three types of solution-relevant inferences, defined a priori by the experimental distribution of two interdependent pieces of information in a dyad: \"Collaborative inferences\" result from unshared, distributed information and \"can only be drawn collaboratively\"; individual
title: A priori taxonomy of three inference types defined by how interdependent information is distributed between collaborators

description: This conceptualization, from Hod and Sagy, categorizes and compares authentic learning scenarios.
title: A taxonomy classifying authentic CSCL learning environments into simulation and hybrid environments with five descriptors

description: The article develops a categorization system for digital providers to enable rigorous estimation of OST tutoring program effects.
title: A taxonomy of digital tutoring defined by tutor location, synchronicity, instruction driver, and curriculum location

description: The article proposes that evaluation of adaptive systems should extend beyond Mark and Greer's goals to \"a new range of evaluative goals which go beyond the quality of learning outcomes, learning efficiency, transfer, retention, and short-term motivation.\" Table 1 lists learner-focused evaluable goa
title: A taxonomy of learner-focused evaluable goals extending outcome, efficiency, transfer, retention and short-term motivation measures

description: The article defines three categories of transitions and tensions between timetabled and non-timetabled learning spaces.
title: A taxonomy of spatial, pedagogic and agentic transitions and tensions between formal and informal learning spaces

description: The article introduces a taxonomy of ten distractor-generation strategies, \"grounded in learning-science literature and empirical observations of LLMs’ reasoning traces\", spanning task understanding (INTER, CORR), candidate construction (LINK, ERR_DESC, ERR_SIM, INST), quality control and selection
title: A ten-strategy taxonomy of distractor-generation strategies grounded in learning-science literature and observed LLM reasoning

description: The article introduces a methodological framework that treats similarity of latent factor structure as a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for transferring score interpretations from humans to LLMs.
title: A validity-oriented framework for comparing assessment latent structure across humans and LLMs
